q: A passenger cancels a reserved ticket which is still on the waitlist, and another cancels one in Reservation Against Cancellation (RAC) status. On such cancellations, the amount deducted from the fare is:

options.A: The prescribed cancellation charge for a confirmed ticket
options.B: Fifty per cent of the fare in every case
options.C: Clerkage charge only
options.D: The reservation charge together with the cancellation charge

e: Under the Coaching Tariff refund rules, waitlisted and RAC tickets have not secured confirmed accommodation, so on cancellation only the clerkage charge is deducted, not the higher cancellation charge prescribed for confirmed tickets.

q: In AC 2-Tier class, the position regarding the bedding supplied to passengers is that:

options.A: It is charged for separately in all trains
options.B: It is supplied free of charge, its cost being included in the fare
options.C: It is not supplied at all
options.D: It is supplied only against a refundable security deposit

e: In AC 2-Tier the cost of bedding is included in the fare itself under the Coaching Tariff, so bed rolls are supplied free and no separate bedding charge is recoverable from the passenger.

q: A low-rated traffic is threatened by road competition, and the Railways agree to carry it at a specially low rate rather than lose it altogether. Under differential pricing in the railway tariff, such a rate may be based on:

options.A: The fully distributed cost of the service in all cases
options.B: The average cost of all coaching and goods services taken together
options.C: The cost of working the most expensive route
options.D: Marginal (out-of-pocket) cost, so long as the traffic makes a contribution towards the fixed costs

e: Differential pricing permits traffic facing road competition to be rated on marginal or out-of-pocket cost, provided the rate covers that cost and contributes something towards fixed costs, rather than on fully distributed cost.

q: The Crew Management System (CMS) of the Railways is used for:

options.A: Booking, rostering and signing-on and signing-off of running staff such as drivers and guards
options.B: Compilation of traffic statistics of crew vans
options.C: Booking of parcel traffic by train crews
options.D: Allotment of quarters to running staff

e: The Crew Management System is the computerised system for booking, rostering, sign-on and sign-off of running staff like drivers and guards, and for monitoring their rest and duty hours.

q: A passenger at a reservation counter asks for a Tatkal booking in a class in which the scheme does not operate at all. The Tatkal scheme for reservation is NOT applicable in:

options.A: AC 2-Tier class
options.B: AC 3-Tier class
options.C: First AC and Executive Class
options.D: Sleeper class

e: The Tatkal scheme under the reservation rules does not operate in First AC and Executive Class; it applies in the other reserved classes including AC 2-Tier, AC 3-Tier and Sleeper, subject to prescribed limits.

q: Besides claims for compensation for goods and for train accidents, the Railway Claims Tribunal also has jurisdiction over claims for:

options.A: Fixation of pay of railway staff
options.B: Refund of fares and freight
options.C: Award of catering contracts at stations
options.D: Allotment of wagons to freight customers

e: Section 13 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 gives the Tribunal jurisdiction, besides goods and accident claims, over claims for refund of fares or freight paid to the railway administration.

q: Which of the following occurrences is also included in the definition of an 'untoward incident' under Section 123 of the Railways Act, 1989?

options.A: Detention of a train on account of fog
options.B: Failure of signalling equipment at a station
options.C: Cancellation of a train for operational reasons
options.D: A terrorist act affecting a passenger in a train or within station premises

e: Section 123(c) of the Railways Act, 1989 defines untoward incident to include a terrorist act, violent attack, robbery, dacoity, rioting or arson affecting a passenger in a train or station premises.

q: A man is found hawking articles for sale inside a train and another is found begging on the platform, neither having any authority to do so. Such unauthorised hawking and begging are prohibited and punishable under:

options.A: Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989 prohibits unauthorised selling of articles and begging in any railway carriage or on railway premises, and makes such hawking and begging punishable.

q: At midnight, a division works out the 'wagon holding' of its railway for the daily position. 'Wagon holding' at any time means:

options.A: The wagons owned by that railway, wherever they may be running
options.B: The wagons loaded at the stations of that railway during the day
options.C: The wagons physically present on the lines of that railway, irrespective of the railway which owns them
options.D: The wagons under repair in the workshops of that railway

e: In operating statistics, wagon holding means all wagons physically present on the lines of a railway at the reporting time, whatever railway owns them; ownership alone does not determine the holding.

q:
A parcel clerk has to select the correct scale of charges according to the train by which a parcel is to be carried. Consider the following statements:
1. The 'P' (Premium) scale is the scale applied to parcels carried by Mail and Express trains.
2. The 'S' (Standard) scale is the scale applied to parcels carried by ordinary passenger trains.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the Coaching Tariff parcel scales, the Premium or P scale applies to parcels carried by Mail and Express trains, while the Standard or S scale applies to parcels carried by ordinary passenger trains.

q: An accounts assistant wonders why the advertisement receipts of his railway are never divided among the other zonal railways. Sundry other earnings are not apportioned among the zonal railways mainly because they:

options.A: Are too small in amount to be apportioned
options.B: Are collected only at the close of the financial year
options.C: Belong to the Railway Board and not to any zonal railway
options.D: Arise locally on a particular railway and are directly identifiable with it, and do not arise from through carriage over several railways

e: Sundry other earnings are not apportioned because they arise locally on one railway and are directly identifiable with it, unlike through coaching and goods earnings which involve carriage over several railways.

q: The earnings reported by a reservation office for a month do not at first agree with the figures received in the Traffic Accounts Office, and a reconciliation is taken up. In that office, the Passenger Reservation System earnings are checked by reconciling them with:

options.A: The remittances and bank credits of the reservation offices for the corresponding period
options.B: The ticket stock register of the reservation office
options.C: The siding statements of the stations concerned
options.D: The handling bills rendered by the stations

e: The Traffic Accounts Office checks PRS earnings for completeness by reconciling them with the remittances made and bank credits received from the reservation offices for the corresponding period.

q: Among the several foils of an Excess Fare Ticket, the foil which is forwarded to the Traffic Accounts Office for check is the:

options.A: Passenger foil
options.B: Guard's foil
options.C: Accounts foil
options.D: Foil retained by the passenger at destination

e: An Excess Fare Ticket has several foils; the Accounts foil is the one sent to the Traffic Accounts Office so that the excess fare collections of ticket checking staff can be checked there.

q: At a small halt station, the man who sells tickets to passengers is not a salaried railway servant but an agent engaged for the purpose. Such halt agents are remunerated by way of:

options.A: A monthly salary paid by the Railways
options.B: Commission on the value of the tickets sold by them
options.C: A share of the station earnings retained by them permanently
options.D: Licence fee paid by the passengers to them

e: Halt agents are not salaried railway servants; under the halt agency terms they are remunerated by commission calculated on the value of the tickets sold by them at the halt station.

q: A commercial officer preparing a case about the losses on an uneconomic branch line asks what the traffic costing figures can establish. Traffic costing data are used by the Railways, among other things, to:

options.A: Fix the pay and allowances of commercial staff
options.B: Allot wagons and rakes to divisions
options.C: Print the Goods Tariff and the Coaching Tariff
options.D: Quantify the losses on uneconomic services and the cost of the social service obligations borne by the Railways

e: Traffic costing data are used to quantify the losses on uneconomic branch lines and services and to work out the cost of social service obligations borne by the Railways, as in costing studies.

q: The 'running speed' of a train, as distinct from its average speed, is computed:

options.A: Excluding the time of halts at intermediate stations en route
options.B: By including the time of halts at all intermediate stations
options.C: By including the detention at the destination terminal
options.D: On the basis of route kilometres divided by the number of trains

e: Running speed is distance divided by actual running time only, excluding halts at intermediate stations; average or commercial speed, by contrast, includes the time of those halts.

q: A parking contractor at a station, asked which department of the Railways awarded his contract, is correctly told that contracts yielding non-fare earnings at stations, such as parking and advertisement contracts, are awarded by the:

options.A: Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: Commercial Department of the Railways
options.C: Accounts Department of the Railways
options.D: Station Master personally

e: Non-fare revenue contracts at stations, such as parking and advertisement contracts, are commercial contracts and are awarded by the Commercial Department, not by Accounts or the Station Master.

q: A logistics operator wants an entire train, and not merely space in a brake van, for moving his parcels between two terminals on a fixed path. Under the Parcel Cargo Express Train service:

options.A: Only the parcel space in the brake van of a passenger train is leased out
options.B: Parcels are carried only by goods trains
options.C: The operator fixes the passenger fares of the train
options.D: A complete parcel train is leased to an operator for running between specified terminals on a time-tabled path

e: Under the Parcel Cargo Express Train scheme a complete parcel train is leased to an operator to run between specified terminals on a time-tabled path, unlike leasing of brake van space alone.

q: A probationer compares the check exercised over station accounts by the Traffic Accounts Office with that exercised by the Railway Audit organisation. As compared with the cent per cent internal check of the Traffic Accounts Office, the statutory audit of station accounts is:

options.A: Also a cent per cent check of every transaction
options.B: Exercised before the transactions take place at the stations
options.C: Confined only to the cash remittances of stations
options.D: A test check exercised on a selective or sample basis

e: The Traffic Accounts Office exercises cent per cent internal check, whereas statutory audit by the Railway Audit organisation is a test check on a selective or sample basis, not a check of every transaction.

q: After floods devastate a district, a relief agency books consignments of relief material for the victims of the calamity. Such consignments are carried by the Railways:

options.A: Free of charge, under the orders of the competent authority
options.B: At double the normal freight rates
options.C: Only on payment of freight in advance in cash
options.D: Only by departmental (material) trains

e: Under the Coaching and Goods Tariff relief provisions, consignments of relief material for victims of a natural calamity are carried free of charge when booked under orders of the competent authority.

q: A statistics clerk compiling the periodical statement of gross earnings of Indian Railways for the Railway Board must start from a basic document. That basic document is the:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Advance Statement of Gross Earnings and Traffic Handled
options.C: Passenger Classification return
options.D: Accounts Office Balance Sheet

e: The periodical statement of gross earnings for Indian Railways is built up from the Advance Statement of Gross Earnings and Traffic Handled furnished by the zonal railways, not from balance sheets.

q:
Consider the following statements about the passenger classification return rendered by a station:
1. The return shows the commencing and closing numbers of the tickets.
2. The return also shows the index numbers of non-issued tickets and the amounts derived from full-fare tickets and concession tickets.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The passenger classification return shows the commencing and closing ticket numbers, the index numbers of non-issued tickets, and the amounts from full-fare and concession tickets, so both statements are correct.

q:
A station accountant asks how corrections to station data are handled after the introduction of the Traffic Accounts Management System (TAMS). Consider the following statements:
1. Under TAMS, the manual submission of station balance sheets continues as before, the system being used only for statistical statements.
2. Under TAMS, every modification in the station data is routed through the Error Sheet module, so that accountal and traceability are ensured.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under TAMS, station balance sheets are computerised and every modification of station data must pass through the Error Sheet module, ensuring proper accountal and traceability; statement 1 is therefore wrong.

q: A booking station has collected amounts that belong to several other stations, and the Traffic Accounts Office has to verify those collections. Such collections made by a station on behalf of other stations are checked with:

options.A: The balance sheets of the collecting station alone
options.B: The cash remittance notes of the collecting station
options.C: The error sheets issued to the collecting station
options.D: The credits taken by those other stations

e: Collections made by a station on behalf of other stations are verified in the Traffic Accounts Office with the credits actually taken by those other stations in their accounts for the same amounts.

q: A passenger who could not undertake his journey surrenders his unused ticket at the station counter and is refunded the fare after deduction of clerkage charges. The document invariably issued to him in connection with this refund is a:

options.A: Money Receipt
options.B: Excess Fare Ticket
options.C: Ticket Deposit Receipt
options.D: Error Sheet

e: When an unused ticket is surrendered at the counter and fare is refunded after deducting clerkage, a Money Receipt is invariably issued to the passenger as the document evidencing that refund.

q:
A station has remitted its day's earnings to the Cash Office and awaits the acknowledgement on the strength of which it will take credit in its Balance Sheet. Consider the following statements:
1. The Cash Office returns one foil of the Cash Remittance Note, signed by the Cashier and the Cash Witness, to the station as an acknowledgement of the cash received from it.
2. It is on the authority of this acknowledgement that the station takes credit for the remittance in its Balance Sheet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Cash Office returns one foil of the Cash Remittance Note, signed by the Cashier and Cash Witness, as acknowledgement, and the station takes credit for the remittance in its Balance Sheet on that authority.

q: A reportable train accident occurs between two stations, and the question arises who must send the first notice of it under the Rules framed under Section 113 of the Railways Act, 1989. The notice is required to be sent, in the first instance, by the:

options.A: Station Master of the destination station of the train
options.B: Station Master nearest to the place where the accident occurred
options.C: Travelling Ticket Examiner of the train
options.D: Chief Claims Officer of the zonal railway

e: Under the rules framed under Section 113 of the Railways Act, 1989, notice of a reportable train accident is first sent by the Station Master nearest to the place where the accident occurred.

q: A claimant dissatisfied with an order of the Railway Claims Tribunal wishes to appeal to the High Court under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987. Such an appeal must be preferred within:

options.A: Ninety days from the date of the order
options.B: Thirty days from the date of the order
options.C: Sixty days from the date of the order
options.D: One year from the date of the order

e: Section 23 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 allows an appeal to the High Court against an order of the Tribunal, to be preferred within ninety days from the date of that order.

q: While examining a proposal to withdraw a loss-making traffic service, a finance officer asks what saving its withdrawal would actually bring. In traffic costing, the 'avoidable cost' of a traffic service means:

options.A: The fully distributed cost of the service, including all overheads
options.B: The cost of the terminals handling the service
options.C: The marginal cost of carrying one additional tonne of traffic
options.D: The cost which would be saved if that service were withdrawn or discontinued

e: In traffic costing, avoidable cost is the cost that would actually be saved if the service were withdrawn or discontinued, excluding costs that would continue despite the withdrawal.

q: An interchange clerk records wagons and traffic passing between his railway and the neighbouring railway at the junction between them. In railway accounts and statistics, traffic so received from, or handed over to, another railway at interchange points is termed:

options.A: Local traffic
options.B: Foreign traffic
options.C: Suburban traffic
options.D: Departmental traffic

e: Traffic received from or handed over to another railway at interchange or junction points is called foreign traffic, as distinct from local traffic originating and terminating on the same railway.

q: A booking clerk works out the fare for a journey and the amount comes to a figure ending in odd paise, which has then to be rounded off before the ticket is issued. Passenger fares on Indian Railways are rounded off:

options.A: To the nearest rupee
options.B: To the next higher multiple of ten rupees
options.C: Without any rounding off, to the exact paise
options.D: To the next higher multiple of five rupees

e: Under the Coaching Tariff, passenger fares are rounded off to the next higher multiple of five rupees after the fare, including applicable charges, has been computed for the journey.

q: A consignee, having taken delivery of goods, argues that the Railway Receipt he surrendered was a negotiable instrument like a cheque. The correct position regarding a Railway Receipt is that it is:

options.A: A negotiable instrument within the meaning of the Negotiable Instruments Act
options.B: A document of title to the goods, transferable by endorsement and delivery, but not a negotiable instrument
options.C: A mere cash receipt for the freight paid
options.D: Valid only in favour of the consignor named on it

e: A Railway Receipt is a document of title to the goods, transferable by endorsement and delivery, but it is not a negotiable instrument within the meaning of the Negotiable Instruments Act.

q: A probationer in the Traffic Accounts Office asks what finally happens to the collected tickets received from stations after their check in that office is complete. After completion of the check, collected tickets are:

options.A: Preserved for the prescribed period and thereafter destroyed under proper authority
options.B: Returned to the passengers who surrendered them
options.C: Sent to the Railway Board for permanent safe custody
options.D: Destroyed at the station immediately after the journey

e: Collected tickets received in the Traffic Accounts Office are preserved for the prescribed retention period after check and are thereafter destroyed under proper authority, as per record rules.

q: A newly posted station master is told to ensure that the public notices required at his station are properly exhibited. Under Section 49 of the Railways Act, 1989, a railway administration is required to exhibit at every station of the railway:

options.A: The list of employees on duty at the station
options.B: The annual accounts of the zonal railway
options.C: A table of the times of arrival and departure of trains and a list of fares payable for travel from the station
options.D: The list of licensed porters engaged at the station

e: Section 49 of the Railways Act, 1989 requires every railway administration to exhibit at each station a table of train arrival and departure times and a list of fares payable from that station.

q: A consignment booked at the owner's risk rate is damaged in transit, and the claimant demands compensation without proving anything against the Railways. Where goods are booked at the owner's risk rate, the railway administration is not liable for loss, destruction, damage or non-delivery unless:

options.A: Negligence or misconduct on the part of the Railways or of their servants is proved by the claimant
options.B: The consignment was insured by the consignor against transit risks
options.C: The consignment was carried in a sealed wagon
options.D: The value of the goods was declared at the time of booking

e: For goods booked at owner's risk rate, Section 98 of the Railways Act, 1989 bars liability for loss or damage unless the claimant proves negligence or misconduct of the Railways or their servants.

q: A passenger travelling between two cities by a day train finds that it has both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned chair car accommodation and that its fares are lower than those of a Shatabdi Express. Such trains are the:

options.A: Duronto Express trains
options.B: Jan Shatabdi Express trains
options.C: Garib Rath Express trains
options.D: Sampark Kranti Express trains

e: Jan Shatabdi Express trains are day trains with both AC and non-AC chair car accommodation, run at fares lower than Shatabdi Express trains for intercity daytime travel.

q: A passenger in an unreserved coach notices cushioned luggage racks, bio-toilets and mobile charging points, and is told the coach is an upgraded general second class coach. Such upgraded unreserved coaches provided on Indian Railways are known as:

options.A: Anubhuti coaches
options.B: Vistadome coaches
options.C: Deen Dayalu coaches
options.D: Mahamana coaches

e: Deen Dayalu coaches are upgraded unreserved general second class coaches provided with amenities like cushioned luggage racks, bio-toilets and mobile charging points for unreserved passengers.

q: A Shatabdi Express carries a premium air-conditioned chair car coach fitted with upgraded amenities for passengers willing to pay a higher fare. Such premium coaches attached to certain Shatabdi Express trains are known as:

options.A: Deen Dayalu coaches
options.B: Anubhuti coaches
options.C: Vistadome coaches
options.D: Tejas coaches

e: Anubhuti coaches are premium AC chair car coaches with upgraded amenities attached to certain Shatabdi Express trains for passengers paying a higher fare than the normal chair car.

q: A passenger books an overnight intercity service and finds that the train is a double-decker with air-conditioned chair car accommodation throughout. Such trains of Indian Railways are the:

options.A: Jan Shatabdi Express trains
options.B: Antyodaya Express trains
options.C: Humsafar Express trains
options.D: UDAY Express trains

e: UDAY Express trains are Utkrisht Double Decker Air-conditioned Yatri services, fully AC double-decker chair car trains introduced for overnight intercity travel.

q: A long-distance train is provided with coaches of an improved design fitted with modern passenger amenities, and the train is run as a model rake service. 'Mahamana' Express trains of Indian Railways are so named because they are provided with:

options.A: 'Model Rake' coaches fitted with modern passenger amenities
options.B: Locomotives manufactured at Banaras Locomotive Works
options.C: Additional coaches reserved for students and teachers
options.D: On-board libraries for the use of passengers

e: Mahamana Express trains use Model Rake coaches fitted with modern passenger amenities and improved interiors, which is the distinguishing feature signified by the Mahamana name.

q: A passenger from a State capital wants a fast direct train to New Delhi and is booked on a service introduced specially to connect the States with the national capital. Such services are the:

options.A: Rajya Rani Express trains
options.B: Jan Shatabdi Express trains
options.C: Sampark Kranti Express trains
options.D: Duronto Express trains

e: Sampark Kranti Express trains were introduced to give State capitals fast direct connectivity with New Delhi, linking the States with the national capital as their special purpose.

q: A passenger travelling from a State capital to another important town within the same State is booked on a train service meant for connectivity inside the State. Such trains are the:

options.A: Sampark Kranti Express trains
options.B: Garib Rath Express trains
options.C: Antyodaya Express trains
options.D: Rajya Rani Express trains

e: Rajya Rani Express trains are meant for connectivity within a State, linking the State capital with other important towns of the same State, rather than with New Delhi.

q: A tourist books a luxury train tour covering the tourist circuits of Rajasthan in royal-style coaches. This luxury tourist train of Indian Railways is the:

options.A: Palace on Wheels
options.B: Maharajas' Express
options.C: Deccan Odyssey
options.D: Fairy Queen

e: Palace on Wheels is the luxury tourist train run in royal style principally on the tourist circuits of Rajasthan, and is the Rajasthan luxury service among the options given.

q: The family of a passenger injured in a train accident needs money at once for treatment and cannot wait till the Railway Claims Tribunal decides the claim. Under Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989, the interim relief payable in such a case, pending determination of the claim, is paid by:

options.A: The Railway Claims Tribunal, out of its own funds
options.B: The railway administration, pending determination of the compensation by the Claims Tribunal
options.C: The State Government of the place where the accident occurred
options.D: The insurance company with which the passenger is insured

e: Section 126 of the Railways Act, 1989 provides for interim relief to an injured passenger or dependants, paid by the railway administration pending determination of compensation by the Claims Tribunal.

q: A claimant who has already received compensation for an accident under the Railways Act files a second claim for the same accident under another law. Under Section 128 of the Railways Act, 1989, a person entitled to compensation for death or injury in a train accident:

options.A: Can claim compensation both under the Railways Act and under any other law for the same accident
options.B: Must claim compensation only through a civil court
options.C: Cannot claim compensation more than once in respect of the same accident
options.D: Cannot claim compensation from the Railways at all

e: Section 128 of the Railways Act, 1989 provides that a person entitled to compensation for death or injury in an accident cannot claim or receive compensation more than once for the same accident.

q: A claimant before the Railway Claims Tribunal objects that his case is being heard without following the full procedure of a civil court. In deciding the claims before it, the Railway Claims Tribunal is:

options.A: Bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure in all respects
options.B: Required to follow the Indian Evidence Act strictly in recording evidence
options.C: Required to dispose of every claim through a full trial like a civil court
options.D: Not bound by the procedure of the Code of Civil Procedure, but is guided by the principles of natural justice

e: Section 18 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 provides that the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and is guided by the principles of natural justice.

q: A trader collects small consignments from a number of small consignors in a town and books them together, in his own name, as a single wagonload consignment. Such a person, in goods traffic, is a:

options.A: Freight forwarder
options.B: Railway servant posted at goods sheds for canvassing traffic
options.C: Siding owner
options.D: Parcel leaseholder

e: A freight forwarder collects small consignments from many small consignors and books them together in his own name as a single wagonload consignment, earning his margin on consolidation.

q: A consignment arrives at destination in a wagon whose seals are found intact, and the consignee demands that it be re-weighed as a matter of right. Where a consignment carried in a sealed wagon arrives with its seals intact, re-weighment of the consignment at the destination:

options.A: Must be granted free of charge as a matter of right
options.B: Cannot be claimed by the consignee as a matter of right
options.C: Can be ordered only by the Railway Claims Tribunal
options.D: Is carried out in all cases at the cost of the Railways

e: Where a sealed wagon arrives with seals intact, there is no presumption of railway fault, so the consignee cannot claim re-weighment at destination as a matter of right under the Goods Tariff.

q: A freight customer registers his demand for wagons through the Freight Operations Information System and then follows the allotment made against it. In FOIS, the module which deals with the allotment of rakes against the demands registered by freight customers is the:

options.A: Terminal Management System
options.B: Rake Management System
options.C: Crew Management System
options.D: Rake Allotment System

e: In FOIS, demands registered by freight customers are dealt with for allotment of rakes through the Rake Allotment System, which matches registered indents with available rake supply.

q: A consignor books a consignment at a station and names himself as the person to whom it is to be delivered at destination. In goods traffic, a consignment is said to be booked to 'Self' when:

options.A: The consignor books the consignment in the name of the Station Master
options.B: The railway administration itself is the consignor of the goods
options.C: The consignor himself is also the consignee of the consignment
options.D: The consignment is booked for carriage by passenger trains

e: A consignment is booked to Self when the consignor himself is also the consignee, so the same person books the goods and takes delivery of them at the destination station.

q: On a busy route, a large number of waitlisted passengers remain unconfirmed day after day, and the Railways run an additional train broadly following the timetable and stoppages of the original train to clear them. Such additional trains are known as:

options.A: Clone trains
options.B: Special trains on Full Tariff Rate
options.C: Holiday special trains
options.D: Examination special trains

e: Clone trains are additional trains run broadly on the timetable and stoppages of the original train to clear the heavy waitlist rush on a busy route, as introduced by the Railways.

q: A heritage special is hauled by a steam locomotive which is claimed to be the oldest of its kind still in working order. The 'Fairy Queen', which is run by Indian Railways on heritage services, is:

options.A: The first diesel locomotive built in India
options.B: The oldest working steam locomotive
options.C: A luxury coach attached to trains for the use of foreign tourists
options.D: The first electric locomotive built at Chittaranjan

e: Fairy Queen is the oldest working steam locomotive, retained and run by Indian Railways on heritage services, which is its recognised distinction in railway heritage records.

q: A tourist books a journey on a luxury train service marketed as one of the finest luxury train experiences in the country. The 'Maharajas' Express' of Indian Railways is:

options.A: A special train run for the use of the President of India
options.B: A train carrying exhibitions on Indian culture to different stations
options.C: A heritage train hauled by the oldest steam locomotive
options.D: A luxury tourist train operated by the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: Maharajas' Express is a luxury tourist train operated by IRCTC and marketed as a premium luxury train experience, distinct from heritage steam or exhibition trains.

q: An engineer working on the high-speed rail project between Mumbai and Ahmedabad is asked which organisation is executing it. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (bullet train) project is being executed by the:

options.A: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited
options.B: National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited
options.C: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited
options.D: Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation

e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project is executed by the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited, the special purpose company set up for high speed rail corridors.

q: A passenger travelling by train places an order on his phone and has food delivered to his seat at a station during the journey. This facility is available to him through:

options.A: The Rail Madad portal of Indian Railways
options.B: The National Train Enquiry System
options.C: The Freight Operations Information System
options.D: The 'e-Catering' service of the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: Food ordered by a passenger to his seat during a journey is supplied through the e-Catering service of IRCTC, using approved vendors at stations en route, not through NTES or FOIS.

q: A ticket checking squad, instead of boarding a train at its starting station, quietly boards it at an unscheduled intermediate point so that ticketless passengers have no warning of the check. Such a check in connection with ticket checking is known as an:

options.A: Fortress check
options.B: Surprise check by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.C: Ambush check
options.D: Block check at the destination station

e: An ambush check is a ticket checking operation in which the squad boards the train quietly at an unscheduled intermediate point, so ticketless passengers get no prior warning of the check.

q: A goods clerk has to work out the wharfage payable on goods lying at his station after unloading. Wharfage charges at a station are levied with reference to:

options.A: The weight of the goods and the period for which they remain on the station premises beyond the free time allowed for their removal
options.B: The number of wagons in which the goods were carried
options.C: A percentage of the freight paid on the consignment
options.D: The value of the goods as declared by the consignee

e: Wharfage is charged under the Goods Tariff on goods not removed from station premises within the free time, with reference to their weight and the period they remain beyond that free time.

q: Two passengers holding Reservation Against Cancellation tickets board a train and are shown to a single berth which they are to share for sitting during the journey. Under the RAC arrangement, the accommodation allotted to the RAC passengers is that:

options.A: Each RAC passenger is allotted a full berth for sleeping
options.B: Two RAC passengers are allotted one side-lower berth to share for sitting
options.C: RAC passengers are accommodated in the general (unreserved) coach
options.D: Each RAC passenger is allotted an upper berth

e: Under the RAC arrangement two RAC passengers are allotted one side-lower berth to share for sitting; a full sleeping berth is given only on confirmation against a vacancy.

q:
Consider the following statements about the accountal of electrical energy consumed on a railway:
1. The energy consumed for hauling trains is accounted for as traction consumption.
2. The energy consumed for other purposes, such as lighting and workshops, is accounted for separately as non-traction consumption.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Electrical energy accountal separates traction consumption, used for hauling trains, from non-traction consumption for lighting, workshops and other purposes, so both statements are correct.

q: A farmer offers live animals for carriage by rail and asks whether they can be booked at the railway risk rate like ordinary goods. Live animals are accepted for carriage by the Railways:

options.A: Only at the railway risk rate
options.B: Only against compulsory payment of the percentage charge
options.C: In wagons owned by the consignor only
options.D: Only at the owner's risk rate

e: Live animals are accepted for carriage only at owner's risk rate under the Goods Tariff, because their condition and behaviour in transit are risks not assumed by the Railways at railway risk.

q:
Consider the following statements about the particulars furnished by a consignor in the Forwarding Note for his consignment:
1. The consignor is responsible for the correctness of the particulars, such as the description and weight of the goods, furnished by him in the Forwarding Note.
2. Where the Railways suffer loss on account of incorrect particulars furnished by the consignor, the loss is recoverable from the consignor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Section 64 and the Forwarding Note conditions, the consignor is responsible for the correctness of particulars furnished, and loss caused to the Railways by incorrect particulars is recoverable from him.

q: A consignor, while his consignment is still in transit, gets its destination changed to a new station, and the goods actually travel by a longer route to reach it. Where a consignment is diverted to a new destination at the request of the consignor, the freight on the consignment is charged:

options.A: For the distance by the route actually followed by the consignment to the new destination
options.B: Only up to the original destination, the onward carriage being free
options.C: At double the normal rate for the diverted portion
options.D: On the basis of the shortest route between the booking station and the new destination, regardless of the route followed

e: When a consignment is diverted at the consignor's request to a new destination, freight is charged for the distance by the route actually followed to that new destination, not the original route.

q: A passenger walks into a computerised reservation centre in a city far away from the place where his train starts and books a berth in that train. This is possible because the Passenger Reservation System of Indian Railways is a countrywide networked system, which means that:

options.A: A passenger can reserve accommodation in any train from any computerised reservation centre, irrespective of the station from which the train starts
options.B: Reservation can be made only at the station from which the train originates
options.C: Reservation centres of one zonal railway cannot book trains of another zonal railway
options.D: Reservation is possible only through the internet and not at counters

e: PRS is a countrywide networked system, so a passenger can reserve accommodation in any train from any computerised reservation centre, regardless of where the train originates.

q: When the reservation chart of a train is being prepared, some confirmed berths fall vacant through cancellations and the passengers holding RAC tickets look forward to getting them. At the time of preparation of the chart, the passengers holding RAC tickets are:

options.A: Treated as waitlisted passengers for all purposes
options.B: Provided confirmed accommodation against the berths falling vacant through cancellations, in the order of their RAC priority
options.C: Refunded the fare automatically
options.D: Required to purchase fresh tickets at the current booking counter

e: At chart preparation, RAC passengers are provided confirmed accommodation against berths falling vacant through cancellations, strictly in the order of their RAC priority.

q: A passenger notes that his long-distance train makes no commercial halt between its originating station and its destination, stopping only for technical purposes. Duronto Express trains were originally introduced by the Railways as:

options.A: Suburban services for metropolitan cities
options.B: Trains carrying only parcels and luggage
options.C: Point-to-point services running between the originating and destination stations without any commercial halt en route, stopping only for technical purposes
options.D: Trains reserved exclusively for the holders of season tickets

e: Duronto Express trains were originally introduced as point-to-point services between origin and destination with no commercial halt en route, stopping only for technical purposes.

q: A passenger who has booked his train ticket online also books a retiring room at his destination station online, without visiting the station. Retiring rooms and dormitories at railway stations can also be booked online through the portal of the:

options.A: Centre for Railway Information Systems
options.B: RailTel Corporation of India
options.C: National Train Enquiry System
options.D: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: Retiring rooms and dormitories at stations can be booked online through the IRCTC portal, in addition to booking at the station, as provided under the IRCTC retiring room facility.

q: A passenger leaves a bag behind in a train, and it is picked up by the railway staff and kept safely for him to claim. Articles left behind by passengers in trains or at stations are deposited in the:

options.A: Lost Property Office of the Railways
options.B: Traffic Accounts Office of the zonal railway
options.C: Parcel office of the destination station, as unclaimed parcels
options.D: Custody of the Travelling Inspector of Accounts

e: Articles left behind by passengers in trains or at stations are deposited in the Lost Property Office of the Railways, from where owners can claim them on proper identification.

q: A statistics clerk compiling the monthly commodity statement of his railway has to show, for the major commodities, the tonnes which began their journey on the railway, those transhipped over it and those which ended their journey on it. Monthly Statistical Statement 7-C of Indian Railways is the statement which gives:

options.A: Passenger and goods train performance, covering tonne kilometres
options.B: Commodity statistics, giving particulars of tonnes originating, transhipped and terminating for the major commodities
options.C: Fuel and power statistics of the railway
options.D: Parcel traffic statistics of the railway

e: Monthly Statistical Statement 7-C is the commodity statement, showing for major commodities the tonnes originating, transhipped and terminating on the railway during the month.

q: A consignor registering his demand for supply of wagons at a station deposits a fee for the registration. The fee deposited by a consignor at the time of registering his demand (indent) for the supply of wagons is known as:

options.A: Wagon Demand Registration Fee
options.B: Wagon Hire Charge
options.C: Siding Deposit Fee
options.D: Demurrage Deposit

e: The fee deposited by a consignor when registering his demand or indent for supply of wagons is the Wagon Demand Registration Fee, distinct from demurrage or wagon hire charges.

q: A patient who has to travel regularly to a distant hospital for dialysis treatment asks the booking clerk whether any concession in rail fare is admissible in his case. Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: All patients travelling to any hospital for indoor treatment
options.B: Persons accompanying a patient as attendant, in all cases
options.C: Kidney patients travelling for dialysis treatment
options.D: Patients travelling for a general health check-up

e: Under the concession rules in the Coaching Tariff, kidney patients travelling for dialysis treatment are admissible for fare concession, subject to the prescribed certificate and conditions.

q: A sports person selected to take part in a tournament at another city asks whether she can get any concession in rail fare for the journey. Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Spectators travelling to witness sporting events
options.B: Owners of sports goods firms travelling on business
options.C: Retired sports persons travelling for personal purposes
options.D: Sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level

e: Fare concession is admissible to sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level, under the prescribed conditions and on production of the required certificate.

q: A passenger tries to book a reserved berth in a train and class in which the maximum prescribed waitlist limit has already been reached, and the system declines any further reservation request for it. When the maximum waitlist limit is so reached, further requests are declined with the status shown as:

options.A: RAC
options.B: PQWL
options.C: REGRET
options.D: TQWL

e: When the maximum prescribed waitlist limit for a train and class is reached, PRS declines further reservation requests and shows the status as REGRET, not RAC or any quota waitlist.

q: A passenger presents a reserved ticket which is torn and mutilated, and asks for a refund at the station. Where a reserved ticket is mutilated or torn, a refund at the station is admissible if:

options.A: The passenger files a Ticket Deposit Receipt in all such cases
options.B: The particulars of the ticket, such as the ticket number and the PNR number, are clearly legible
options.C: The passenger pays a duplicate ticket charge
options.D: The reservation chart of the train has not been prepared

e: Refund on a mutilated or torn reserved ticket is admissible at the station if its particulars, such as ticket number and PNR number, are clearly legible so the booking can be verified.

q: A passenger who does not wish to visit the station merely to buy a platform ticket books a paperless platform ticket on his phone. A paperless platform ticket can be booked by a passenger through:

options.A: The IRCTC website only
options.B: The NTES application only
options.C: The UTS mobile application
options.D: The Rail Madad portal

e: A paperless platform ticket can be booked through the UTS mobile application, which issues mobile tickets for unreserved travel and platform tickets without a paper printout.

q: A goods clerk explains to a consignee that the longer his wagons remain detained beyond the free time, the higher the rate at which demurrage will be charged on them. Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed are levied:

options.A: At a flat rate for all periods of detention
options.B: Only for the first day of detention
options.C: At rates which decrease as the period of detention lengthens
options.D: At rates which increase (escalate) as the period of detention lengthens

e: Demurrage under the Goods Tariff is levied at escalating rates as detention of wagons beyond free time lengthens, to discourage prolonged detention and secure quicker release of wagons.

q: A zonal railway's statement showing its local traffic earnings alongside the through traffic earnings that must be shared with other railways is not prepared daily or at year-end; the Traffic Book in which these figures are brought together is compiled:

options.A: Monthly
options.B: Every ten days
options.C: Quarterly
options.D: Annually

e: The Traffic Book, which brings together local earnings and through earnings to be apportioned between railways, is compiled monthly for each zonal railway in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: A container operator objects to his bill being worked out tonne by tonne under the ordinary commodity classification. For container traffic, haulage charges are correctly levied:

options.A: At wagonload class rates for the wagon used
options.B: Per container, in TEU or FEU terms, and not on the commodity classification and tonne basis of ordinary goods traffic
options.C: At the parcel scales in force
options.D: Per tonne, on the classification applicable to ordinary goods traffic

e: For container traffic, haulage charges are levied per container in TEU or FEU terms under the container tariff, not per tonne on the commodity classification of ordinary goods traffic.

q: An IRCTC product sold at stations yields receipts which the station accountant proposes to credit to the Railways as coaching earnings. Receipts from the sale of 'Rail Neer' packaged drinking water belong to:

options.A: The Railways, as sundry other earnings
options.B: The station staff welfare fund
options.C: IRCTC, and do not form part of the traffic earnings of the Railways
options.D: The Railways, as coaching earnings

e: Rail Neer is an IRCTC product and its sale receipts belong to IRCTC; they are not credited as coaching or sundry traffic earnings of the Railways in station accounts.

q: The figures of approximate gross earnings furnished by the individual zonal railways for each ten-day period are consolidated for Indian Railways as a whole:

options.A: By each station for its own earnings
options.B: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year
options.D: In the Railway Board, by aggregating the figures furnished by the zonal railways

e: Approximate gross earnings for ten-day periods furnished by zonal railways are consolidated for Indian Railways as a whole in the Railway Board by aggregating the zonal figures.

q: When the siding statement of a station reaches the Traffic Accounts Office, the check applied to it is directed at seeing that:

options.A: The siding charges and demurrage due for the wagons placed in and removed from the sidings have been correctly levied and fully brought to account
options.B: The siding staff are correctly paid their wages
options.C: The wagons owned by the siding owner are repaired in time
options.D: The total earnings of the station agree with the Cash Office figures

e: Check of the siding statement in the Traffic Accounts Office ensures that siding charges and demurrage for wagons placed in and removed from sidings have been correctly levied and fully accounted.

q: In checking the earnings reported through the Passenger Reservation System, the Traffic Accounts Office establishes their completeness by reconciling them with:

options.A: The ticket stock register of the reservation office
options.B: The remittances and bank credits of the reservation offices for the corresponding period
options.C: The siding statements of the stations concerned
options.D: The handling bills rendered by the stations

e: Completeness of PRS earnings is established in the Traffic Accounts Office by reconciling them with the remittances and bank credits of the reservation offices for the corresponding period.

q: An Excess Fare Ticket book has several foils for each ticket; the foil which the ticket checking staff forward to the Traffic Accounts Office so that the collections can be checked there is the:

options.A: Passenger foil
options.B: Guard's foil
options.C: Accounts foil
options.D: Foil retained by the passenger at destination

e: Of the foils of an Excess Fare Ticket, the Accounts foil is forwarded by ticket checking staff to the Traffic Accounts Office so that the excess fare collections can be checked there.

q: Coaching and goods earnings of through traffic are shared between railways, but sundry other earnings are kept out of that sharing mainly because they:

options.A: Are too small in amount to be apportioned
options.B: Are collected only at the close of the financial year
options.C: Belong to the Railway Board and not to any zonal railway
options.D: Arise locally on a particular railway and are directly identifiable with it, and do not arise from through carriage over several railways

e: Sundry other earnings are kept out of apportionment because they arise locally on a particular railway and are directly identifiable with it, and do not arise from through carriage over several railways.

q: Apart from guiding fare and freight fixation, the traffic costing figures compiled by the Railways are also put to use to:

options.A: Quantify the losses on uneconomic services and the cost of the social service obligations borne by the Railways
options.B: Fix the pay and allowances of commercial staff
options.C: Allot wagons and rakes to divisions
options.D: Print the Goods Tariff and the Coaching Tariff

e: Besides fare and freight fixation, traffic costing figures are used to quantify losses on uneconomic services and the cost of social service obligations borne by the Railways.

q: A parking contractor at a station claims his contract was awarded by the Accounts Department. Contracts yielding non-fare earnings at stations, such as parking and advertisement contracts, are in fact awarded by the:

options.A: Traffic Accounts Office
options.B: Commercial Department of the Railways
options.C: Accounts Department of the Railways
options.D: Station Master personally

e: Parking, advertisement and similar non-fare earning contracts at stations are commercial contracts awarded by the Commercial Department, not by the Traffic Accounts Office or Accounts Department.

q: The internal check of station accounts in the Traffic Accounts Office covers every transaction, whereas the statutory audit of the same accounts by the Railway Audit organisation is:

options.A: Also a cent per cent check of every transaction
options.B: Exercised before the transactions take place at the stations
options.C: A test check exercised on a selective or sample basis
options.D: Confined only to the cash remittances of stations

e: Statutory audit of station accounts by the Railway Audit organisation is a test check on a selective or sample basis, unlike the cent per cent internal check in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: Leasing the space in a brake van of a passenger train is different from the Parcel Cargo Express Train service, under which:

options.A: Only the parcel space in the brake van of a passenger train is leased out
options.B: Parcels are carried only by goods trains
options.C: The operator fixes the passenger fares of the train
options.D: A complete parcel train is leased to an operator for running between specified terminals on a time-tabled path

e: Under the Parcel Cargo Express Train service a complete parcel train is leased to an operator between specified terminals on a time-tabled path, unlike mere leasing of brake van space.

q: After floods devastate a district, a relief organisation tenders medicines and food packets for carriage to the affected area and asks what freight will be charged on them. Relief consignments of this kind, booked for victims of a natural calamity, are carried by the Railways:

options.A: Free of charge, under the orders of the competent authority
options.B: At double the normal freight rates
options.C: Only on payment of freight in advance in cash
options.D: Only by departmental (material) trains

e: Relief consignments like medicines and food for victims of a natural calamity are carried free of charge under the tariff relief provisions, when booked under orders of the competent authority.

q: A statistics clerk must pick the monthly statement that reports how passenger trains have performed, as distinct from the one for goods trains. Monthly Statistical Statement 1 of Indian Railways relates to:

options.A: Goods train performance
options.B: Passenger train performance
options.C: Fuel and power statistics
options.D: Commodity statistics

e: Monthly Statistical Statement 1 of Indian Railways relates to passenger train performance, while goods train performance is covered by the corresponding separate statement for goods services.

q: A siding owner argues that, because the Railways use his siding for their traffic, they should share the cost of building it. The entire cost of construction of a private siding is borne by:

options.A: The Railways entirely
options.B: The Railways and the siding owner in equal shares
options.C: The siding owner entirely
options.D: The State Government

e: The entire cost of construction of a private siding is borne by the siding owner, since the siding is provided for his exclusive use, though it is built to railway standards and specifications.

q: At the start of an earning contract at a station, the contractor deposits security money with the Railways. That security deposit is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways in all cases
options.B: Treated as a traffic earning of the station
options.C: Refunded on the very day the contract is awarded
options.D: Retained during the currency of the contract and refunded after its satisfactory completion and clearance of dues

e: Security deposit taken from an earning contractor is retained during the currency of the contract and refunded only after satisfactory completion of the contract and clearance of all dues.

q: Before a handling bill rendered by a station is passed for payment, the Traffic Accounts Office verifies it mainly with reference to:

options.A: The rates in the handling contract and the certified quantities of goods and parcels handled
options.B: The pay bills of the goods shed staff
options.C: The earnings of the station for the month
options.D: The number of wagons allotted to the station

e: A handling bill is passed in the Traffic Accounts Office after verification with the rates in the handling contract and the certified quantities of goods and parcels actually handled.

q: Rent-like receipts come to a station from many small contracts; the licence fees recovered for the bookstalls provided at stations are accounted under:

options.A: Other coaching earnings
options.B: Sundry other earnings
options.C: Goods earnings
options.D: Capital receipts

e: Licence fees for bookstalls at stations are non-fare receipts arising locally at stations and are accounted under sundry other earnings, not under coaching, goods or capital receipts.

q: The Railways quote special Station-to-Station rates for selected pairs of stations, departing from the general tariff, primarily in order to:

options.A: Fix a uniform rate for all stations of the railway
options.B: Charge parcels moving between the nominated stations
options.C: Attract and retain specified traffic between the nominated stations, particularly against road competition
options.D: Replace the Goods Tariff for all traffic

e: Station-to-Station rates are quoted under the Goods Tariff to attract and retain specified traffic between nominated stations, particularly traffic threatened by road competition.

q: Unlike a terminal built for one party's exclusive traffic, a Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal is a:

options.A: Terminal confined to the traffic of the developer alone
options.B: Terminal meant only for parcel traffic
options.C: Terminal provided only for the traffic of Government departments
options.D: Common-user cargo terminal, open for handling the traffic of all freight customers and not confined to the developer's own traffic

e: A Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal is a common-user terminal open to the traffic of all freight customers, and is not confined to the developer's own traffic like an exclusive terminal.

q: The Parcel Management System used for parcel traffic primarily provides:

options.A: Bar-coding of parcels and their end-to-end tracking from booking to delivery
options.B: Compilation of the Station Balance Sheet
options.C: Allotment of wagons against indents
options.D: Preparation of reservation charts

e: The Parcel Management System provides bar-coding of parcels and their end-to-end tracking from booking to delivery, improving accountal and customer information for parcel traffic.

q:
A cement major is negotiating a Long Term Tariff Contract and asks what the contract offers him in return for the traffic he assures. Consider the following statements in this regard:
1. The customer gets stability of freight rates for the period of the contract.
2. The customer earns incentives linked to the growth of traffic over the agreed level.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under a Long Term Tariff Contract the customer gets freight rate stability for the contract period and incentives linked to growth of traffic above the agreed level, so both statements are correct.

q: An operator who invests in special-purpose rakes under the Special Freight Train Operator scheme must, besides making that investment:

options.A: Fix the freight rates for all customers of the Railways
options.B: Hand over his entire earnings to the Railways
options.C: Pay haulage charges to the Railways for the movement of his rakes over the railway network
options.D: Maintain the railway track used by his rakes

e: Under the Special Freight Train Operator scheme the operator invests in special-purpose rakes and pays haulage charges to the Railways for movement of those rakes over the railway network.

q: A passenger who has been overcharged does not have to go to a civil court for the money; besides claims for goods and for compensation for train accidents, the Railway Claims Tribunal also has jurisdiction over claims for:

options.A: Fixation of pay of railway staff
options.B: Award of catering contracts at stations
options.C: Allotment of wagons to freight customers
options.D: Refund of fares and freight

e: Section 13 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 gives the Tribunal jurisdiction over claims for refund of fares and freight, so an overcharged passenger need not go to a civil court.

q: A man is found hawking eatables inside a train without authority and another is found begging on the platform. Unauthorised hawking and begging in a train or on railway premises are prohibited and punishable under:

options.A: Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 137 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Section 144 of the Railways Act, 1989 prohibits and punishes unauthorised hawking of articles and begging in a train or on railway premises, covering both acts described in the question.
